messages.author: e19ea506112fd25b
messages.subject: rstan on regulated windows PCs
parts:
Hi,

In our university users are not allowed to modify contents of any folder except on C:\TEMP.  Personal files are stored on the network.  Is it possible to tell rstan to use different locations (preferably c:\TEMP) for temporary files where compiled etc code and data are stored?

Thanks for any suggestions,
Linas

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: rstan on regulated windows PCs
parts:
The stan_model() function writes to whatever tempdir() is, so if that does not correspond to C:\TEMP, then your .Rprofile should set the environmental variables described in help(tempdir).

Ben

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: rstan on regulated windows PCs
parts:
Has it worked on that PC before?. The status 127 code is for program not found errors

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/1763156/127-return-code-from

So, it would appear as if Rtools is not set up correctly. Remember that in the Rtools installer there is a set where it asks you whether you want to modify the PATH, and you have to check the box, which may require administrative privlidges.

Ben
